statement: Each worker sends a heartbeat to the host every `heartbeat.everyMs`.

events.why: The default comes from RFC 0001's kernel config; ADR 0001 kept it when it set where isolates run.
The supervisor wired to real workers, built in M1.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: A worker with no beat for `blockedAfterMs` marks its isolates `blocked`, and their surfaces show the busy overlay. Nothing is restarted.

events.why: The default comes from RFC 0001's kernel config; ADR 0001 kept it when it set where isolates run.
The supervisor's state machine, built in M1.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: A worker with no beat for `killAfterMs` is terminated, and its isolates crash with reason `unresponsive`.

events.why: The default comes from RFC 0001's kernel config; ADR 0001 kept it when it set where isolates run.
The supervisor's state machine, built in M1.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: An isolate that sends no `ready` within `readyTimeoutMs` of its spawn crashes with reason `ready_timeout`.

events.why: The default comes from RFC 0001's kernel config; ADR 0001 kept it when it set where isolates run.
The supervisor's state machine, built in M1.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: An isolate that crashes after `maxRestarts` restarts within `withinMs` is `failed`: the kernel emits `isolate:failed`, its surface shows the fallback, and the rest of the app keeps running.

events.why: The default comes from RFC 0001's kernel config; ADR 0001 kept it when it set where isolates run.
The supervisor's state machine, built in M1.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: A crash after a healthy run shorter than 60 s, from `ready` to the last beat, counts toward `maxRestarts` however long the runs took. A crash after a longer run clears the count first. The isolate fails on this rule or the sliding window, whichever is met first. The bus worker follows the same rule.

events.why: A crash loop slower than the window never reached `failed`: #390 measured isolates that hung 10 s after each start still restarting after 150 s.
Built on main; backported to release/0.1 in #439.
First released in 0.1.1.

statement: `supervisor.healthyAfterMs` is the healthy run that clears the count of short runs. `withinMs` is the sliding window only, and either may be the larger. It applies to the bus worker too.

events.why: One number was both the window and the healthy run, so an app couldn't widen one without the other. The 0.2 codemod sets it beside an existing `withinMs`.
Built on main; ships in 0.2.0.

statement: `healthyAfterMs` must be a positive integer, with no upper limit. Any other value makes `createKernel` throw `invalid_config`.

events.why: A malformed option fails at start, as other options do.
Built on main; ships in 0.2.0.

statement: Each restart waits `initialMs × factorⁿ`, capped at `maxMs`, where n is the larger of the window count and the short-run count. *Retry* clears both.

events.why: The default comes from RFC 0001's kernel config; ADR 0001 kept it when it set where isolates run.
The supervisor's state machine, built in M1.
First released in 0.1.0.
With a second count, the backoff follows whichever count is larger; shipped in 0.1.1.
events.prev: Each restart waits `initialMs × factorⁿ`, capped at `maxMs`, where n is the restart count.

statement: `isolate:failed`'s `message` names the rule that was met, for example "3 restarts in 60000 ms" or "4 crashes, each after less than 60000 ms of healthy running".

events.why: With two rules, a reader needs to know which one failed the isolate.
Built on main; backported to release/0.1 in #439.
First released in 0.1.1.

statement: The heartbeat kill and the ready timeout measure silence on a lag clock: `performance.now()` minus the total time the host's 50 ms supervision tick fired late. Time in which the host couldn't hear a beat doesn't count. The bus worker's timers use it too.

events.why: On a CPU-starved page the host itself is late, so a worker waiting for a CPU looked hung and was killed. The lag clock removed every false kill at the defaults in the spike.
Built on main; ships in 0.2.0.

statement: A worker silent for 3 × `killAfterMs` of wall-clock time is killed whatever the lag clock says. The ready timeout has the same cap on its own limit, 3 × `readyTimeoutMs`. The factor isn't an option.

events.why: A hung worker on a starved page must still be killed, at most 3 times later than on a page that isn't starved.
Built on main; ships in 0.2.0.

statement: Only the heartbeat kill and the ready timeout use the lag clock. `blockedAfterMs`, the restart window, the healthy run and the backoff stay on wall-clock time.

events.why: The busy overlay and the restart limit keep behaving as they did; the #390 crash loop still fails at the same crash.
Built on main; ships in 0.2.0.

statement: For `readyTimeoutMs` after an isolate's `ready`, a blocked isolate is killed only after `readyTimeoutMs` without a beat, not `killAfterMs`.

events.why: Plant's restart loop on Firefox CI looked like start-up work killed by a short `killAfterMs`.
Never built (#384 closed unmerged), and the loop came from the tests, not start-up. It also weakened the restart limit (#390).
What a CPU-starved worker needs went back to its issue.
Replaced by the lag clock; nothing from #384 is reused.

statement: The supervisor doesn't judge a silent worker against its siblings (holding kills while most workers are silent).

events.why: Why not hold a kill while most workers are silent? Measured, it removed only 0 to 9 % of the false kills and delayed the kill of a hang that hits half the workers or more.

statement: Workers don't send a beat counted in CPU time.

events.why: Why not count a worker's CPU time instead? A worker that doesn't get a CPU can't send that beat either.

statement: When the count of live workers passes the soft budget, the kernel warns once with `workers:budget`. A pool counts as one worker. The budget never refuses a spawn or suspends an isolate.

events.why: The real ceiling depends on the device, so the budget is a hint, not a guarantee.
Loader hardening, built in M1.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: If the browser fails to create a worker, the isolate crashes with reason `spawn_failed` and gets the usual backoff and restart limit. Before each retry the supervisor suspends every idle suspendable isolate, to free memory.

events.why: Memory runs out on the device, not at a count Isoloop can know, so a failed spawn is handled like any crash.
Loader hardening, built in M1.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The worker budget isn't derived from the device (for example cores × 4).

events.why: Why not scale the budget to the device? Browser-reported figures are coarse or hidden, and the warning would differ per machine.

statement: There is no hard limit on the number of workers.

events.why: Why not refuse spawns past a limit? It fails apps on capable machines and still doesn't protect weak ones.

statement: Passing the worker budget doesn't suspend isolates. Memory is freed only after a real `spawn_failed`.

events.why: Why not suspend isolates once the budget is passed? It would turn a warning into behaviour.

statement: While `document.hidden` is true, the supervisor doesn't judge hangs: no busy overlay and no kills. Worker errors are still handled.

events.why: Background tabs throttle main-thread timers, so beats look late when they aren't.
The supervisor wired to real workers, built in M1.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: On `visibilitychange` to visible and on the Page Lifecycle `resume` event, every heartbeat clock, the isolates' and the bus worker's, restarts from zero.

events.why: Returning to a tab must never kill an isolate for beats missed while it was hidden or frozen.
The supervisor wired to real workers, built in M1.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The bus worker sends `beat` on its control port, and the supervisor judges it with the same blocked and kill timeouts as an isolate. The kernel emits `bus:ready { first }`, `bus:crash`, `bus:restart` and `bus:failed`.

events.why: The bus worker holds every topic log and offset, so it gets the same supervision as an isolate.
The host's bus controller and its supervision, built in M2.
First released in 0.1.0.

statement: The bus worker restarts under the kernel's `supervisor` config, like an isolate. Past the limit the kernel emits `bus:failed`; isolates keep running, and every publish rejects with `bus_unavailable`.

events.why: Same limit as an isolate, so a bus that keeps crashing ends in a state the app can show.
The host's bus controller and its supervision, built in M2.
Found while writing the supervision guide (#320): an app that sets `supervisor` sets it for the bus worker too.
events.prev: Up to 3 restarts in 60 s, read as a fixed limit.

events.why: First released in 0.1.0.
